transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (Gateway Head of Partnerships), Tom Becker (Gateway VP Sales), Sana Patel (Gateway Solutions Architect)

Summary: quick ops playbook review for co-sell, align pilots and data/compliance gating, clarify responsibilities. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted economics, regional data residency, and top account prioritization. Agreed next steps and action owners.

00:00:05 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — should we do quick intros?
00:00:18 - Elena Ruiz: Hi, Elena here — running partnerships for Gateway, been talking with Maya over email.
00:00:25 - Tom Becker: Tom, VP Sales, curious on how we scale pilots across our payer accounts.
00:00:31 - Maya Chen: Great. Liam, want to give a quick ops/arch summary before we jump to account mapping?
00:00:37 - Liam O'Connor: Yeah sure. So from Redwood side — we typically recommend starting with either our hosted API for speed or Dedicated reserved capacity if you need strict throughput and isolation. For regulated accounts we can do Private (VPC) but there's on-prem options too.
00:00:55 - Sana Patel: quick Q — for the VPC/private option, does data ever leave the customer's region? We have EU accounts with strict residency.
00:01:05 - Liam O'Connor: Good question. For Private we co-manage the control plane; data egress stays in-region per the deployment. For Hosted, we do region pinning but you'll want to check contract for explicit residency commitments.
00:01:18 - Tom Becker: And what about latency? Some of our workflows are near-real time in clinical workflows — 300-400ms is around our target.
00:01:29 - Liam O'Connor: So depends on model size and sequence length — our optimized kernels and batching target sub-300ms for common gen workloads on Dedicated; hosted can be similar but at very high QPS you might see variable tail latencies unless you reserve capacity.
00:01:48 - Elena Ruiz: We also need to know how billing will surface to our channel metrics — is it per-token direct, or can we resell?
00:01:57 - Maya Chen: We have a channel pricing grid we can share — there's resell/commit structures for partners. I'll send the draft joint-deck and pricing grid after the call.
00:02:06 - Tom Becker: Perfect.

00:02:40 - Speaker 1: (inaudible) — sorry, there's a quick echo, Liam can you re-share the chart about dedicated throughput?
00:02:50 - Liam O'Connor: Sure, I'll paste the link in chat — same spreadsheet we used in the last benchmark. Note: benchmarks are representative — actual latency depends on prompt patterns and KV cash usage — sorry KV cache, transcription glitch there, KV cache.
00:03:09 - Maya Chen: (laughs) we get a lot of weird transcriptions.

00:04:05 - Liam O'Connor: High level ops playbook idea: 1) Identify pilot accounts (top 5 prioritized) 2) Design pilot SLAs and success metrics (latency, cost per session, UX acceptance) 3) Decide deployment mode per pilot (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) 4) Run 2-week tech validation and 6-week business pilot.
00:04:33 - Elena Ruiz: That matches what we wanted. For prioritization, we want co-sell deals where Gateway owns the channel and we have legal/contracting leverage.
00:04:45 - Tom Becker: Also need clarity on audit logs and SSO — SOC2 level audit trail and SAML/Okta integration for our end users.
00:04:55 - Liam O'Connor: We support SAML SSO and have audit logging; for Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. We'll add a slide on that.

00:06:12 - Sana Patel: On the tech side, two pain points: (1) We want predictable token costs per call for pricing reconciliations, (2) model fallbacks if a large request spikes costs but we need graceful degradation.
00:06:27 - Maya Chen: For cost predictability we can use reserved Dedicated slots and apply caching to reduce token counts; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization or model variants to pull down unit costs.
00:06:40 - Tom Becker: When you say model variants — does that mean lower-accuracy but cheaper models for heavy scale?
00:06:46 - Liam O'Connor: Exactly — we can route to a cheaper quantized variant or shorter context model when the request meets certain heuristics, with automatic fallback to higher-quality model if results fail checks.
00:07:02 - Elena Ruiz: legal will ask about data retention windows and ability to purge. Can Redwood guarantee deletion on request?
00:07:10 - Maya Chen: Yes, we have configurable retention and purge APIs for Private/Dedicated — for Hosted we can offer contract-level terms and support e-discovery requests. We'll share the security packet.

00:08:35 - Tom Becker: Competitor question — we had a pilot with Nimbus AI last year and they underperformed on throughput and had opaque cost. How do you help with observability?
00:08:45 - Liam O'Connor: Our Console shows token-level breakdowns, per-route latency, and tracing hooks, plus rollout controls for canary and A/B. That transparency is a big difference.
00:08:58 - Elena Ruiz: Can you map that to our CRM so we can attribute closed-won to partner-sourced leads? That's important.
00:09:07 - Maya Chen: We can add CRM tagging patterns in the joint-deck and the spreadsheet; we'll propose fields for attribution.

00:10:30 - (30 seconds of side conversation confirming spreadsheet link pasted)
00:10:55 - Liam O'Connor: Going back to pilots — we recommend starting with one Hosted pilot and one Dedicated pilot if you have two different account profiles (non-regulated vs regulated). This gives a clear comparison.
00:11:12 - Sana Patel: For the Dedicated pilot, how long does provisioning take? We have a two-week window ideally.
00:11:20 - Liam O'Connor: Provisioning Dedicated reserved pools typically 5-7 business days with templates; Private/VPC can take longer depending on network approvals.

00:12:45 - Tom Becker: Let's talk risk: what are the failure modes? e.g., if model outputs unexpectedly regress and product quality drops mid-pilot.
00:12:55 - Maya Chen: We pair Redwood Optimize with evals — define a prompt set to monitor, set regression alerts, and automatic rollback to previous model versions. We'll also run quality checks pre-cutover.
00:13:12 - Elena Ruiz: Good. Also can you provide legal proof points — SOC2, ISO?
00:13:18 - Maya Chen: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO certs are in our security packet. We'll attach them to the shared drive.

00:14:35 - Speaker labels get fuzzy here, small crosstalk: "...yeah, and if we can set up the pricing…"

00:15:10 - Liam O'Connor: Quick numbers — for a medium conversational workload, Dedicated reserved commitment can reduce unit cost by ~30% vs pay-as-you-go hosted, depending on throughput. Exact math is in the TCO sheet.
00:15:27 - Tom Becker: That 30% assumes similar latency?
00:15:32 - Liam O'Connor: Yes, assuming you size capacity to avoid queuing. If you underprovision, tail latency goes up. That's why autoscale and burst policies matter.

00:17:02 - Elena Ruiz: For go-to-market, our channel SDRs need a one-pager and battlecard. Can Redwood produce one?
00:17:10 - Maya Chen: We'll draft a channel one-pager and partner battlecard. Put that as an action item.

00:18:45 - (discussion about mapping top accounts begins)
00:18:58 - Sana Patel: I'll upload our top 10 accounts CSV to the shared folder — it includes account type and any specialist compliance notes.
00:19:08 - Maya Chen: Great, Gateway — once we get that we can recommend which deployment each account should use and an initial pilot candidate list.

00:21:30 - Tom Becker: Quick commercial ask — we need a draft MSA or reseller amendment to present to legal.
00:21:38 - Maya Chen: We have a partner MSA template — we'll include it with the security packet.

00:23:05 - (technical micro-deep dive led by Liam; some timestamps where Liam reads kernel/quant notes)
00:23:20 - Liam O'Connor: On kernel selection — we choose optimized kernels based on model family and sequence length. In practice that means if your prompts are short the throughput goes way up; if they're long we pick a different memory path. This is why real workload tests are essential.
00:24:05 - Sana Patel: Can we schedule a 1-hour technical POC to run a representative query set?
00:24:12 - Liam O'Connor: Yes — we'll do that in the tech kickoff. We request sample prompts and a recent session log for more realistic results.

00:26:30 - (short silence, then planning next steps)
00:26:44 - Elena Ruiz: So to recap: Redwood will send pricing, joint-deck, security packet, partner MSA, and TCO spreadsheet. Gateway will send top 10 accounts and compliance notes, and confirm internal channel lead.
00:27:02 - Tom Becker: And then a POC kickoff week of Feb 9th?
00:27:08 - Maya Chen: That's the plan. We'll propose exact times after we share availability.

00:27:50 - (question from Tom re: evaluation metrics)
00:27:56 - Maya Chen: We'll propose success criteria: latency under 350ms p95, cost per session below X (we'll calculate after we see sample traffic), and user acceptance > 80% on manual QA checks.

00:29:30 - (wrap up, minor small talk)
00:30:00 - Maya Chen: Any blockers from legal or compliance we should know about right now?
00:30:06 - Elena Ruiz: Legal will want the MSA and the SOC docs; procurement will want clear billing terms for channel attribution.
00:30:14 - Maya Chen: We'll include both items.

00:30:40 - (final confirmations)
00:31:00 - Maya Chen: Okay thanks everyone. We'll send the packet and set up the tech kickoff.

Action items (as read during call):
- Maya Chen: Send co-sell pricing grid + draft joint-deck (due 2026-02-02)
- Liam O'Connor: TCO slide + latency bench + provisioning runbook (due 2026-02-04)
- Sana Patel: Upload top 10 accounts + compliance notes to shared folder (due 2026-02-05)
- Elena Ruiz: Confirm internal channel lead and go/no-go criteria (due 2026-02-06)

Questions raised:
- Data residency guarantees for Private deployments (answered: yes, can be region-pinned)
- Ability to purge retained data on request (answered: yes via purge APIs, contract support for Hosted)
- Integration points for CRM attribution (answered: yes, will propose tagging patterns)

Recording notes: some transcription artifacts in tech sections — e.g., "K V cash" instead of KV cache, minor speaker mis-attributions.

End of transcript.
